recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce a core CodeSystem duplicate; any future edits to this code system should go through UTG/THO.
issue_request: FHIR-22742 was Applied with resolution Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core AdverseEvent. It requested a code system description of "This code system contains methods for assessing causality" and definitions for probability-scale, bayesian, and checklist/check-list.
initial_application: No core FHIR commit explicitly mentioned FHIR-22742. Current core source keeps AdverseEvent and its adverse-event-causality-method ValueSet in build scope, but that ValueSet composes from http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/adverse-event-causality-method. The prior duplicate core CodeSystem had a TODO description and no concept definitions, then was deleted by the THO duplicate-removal commit a3768d9df82b8b5b5b7bedfbe08618ea365d9b2f before this Jira was applied.
additional_context: FHIR-22742 led to UP-598, a Patient Care-sponsored UTG proposal with the same requested code system description and concept definitions. UP-598 is Proposal Implemented, THO release notes list it as published in THO version 6.2.0, and both THO 6.2.0 and current CodeSystem XML contain the requested definitions. The Jira prose sometimes writes check-list, but the pre-existing code is checklist and UP-598 preserved that code while adding the definition.
reconciliation: Created an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. No core source change was made because the authoritative code system source is external to the FHIR core checkout and the external terminology content referenced by core is already correct.

related_jiras.note: UTG proposal that implemented the code system description and concept definitions requested by FHIR-22742.
